log.msg: Layout answers. The picker overlay and the floating ? are fixed to the viewport, in no page container; the ? is a 2.4em circle and the panel is min(26em, 100vw - 2em) wide with the chat list scrolling inside, so both are controls sized in their own em, never in --gap. The chip is one nowrap flex row inside the chat's existing column. The demo section sits in the page's main track.

Trap found before it bit: Page.css makes a containing block for position:fixed on any page with a rail (:has(> .rail)) and on every columns host, so a float captured inside such a page pins to that region's corner instead of the viewport's. It degrades to the same place visually, so mount() stays captured in the page (page lifetime for free) rather than escaping to document.body and leaking across navigation.

No cycle: pick.js imports only View; Ask.js imports pick.js for describe(); chat.js imports both. That is why mount() ships from chat.js and not from Ask.js -- Ask.js re-exporting chat.js would be the parent-child import cycle CLAUDE.md warns breaks on deep reload.

new-css-class: ask- is a NEW namespace; the census of .ask-pick .ask-float .ask-chip across every css and js under public/ is empty. css-scopes.txt is outside the fence, so the reservation line goes into doc/decisions.md under Open for whoever can write it.

assign.now: built and proven; writing the docs

log.msg: The page url found by the nearest .page ancestor is NOT where the readme is. On /framework/ext/Ask/ a Doc renders content into a synthetic child page, so the first pick reported /framework/ext/Ask/overview/intro/ and found no readme at all. context() now climbs at most three rungs of the path and stops at the first readme.md; the readout names the url it used, so a surprising answer is visible instead of silent.

The css-scopes.txt prefix lookup EARNS its lines, measured on seven elements of one page: .tab-bar -> ext/tabs/readme.md, .dev-bar -> dev/DevBar/readme.md, .page-previews -> core/Page/readme.md. Three of seven got a component readme the page readme could never have given. It costs one cached fetch of a 4k text file and about twelve lines.

No server change was needed. The element context rides in the PROMPT, not in the system line: Server/plugins/Ask.js slices `context` to 800 characters for the system prompt and a readme is 2.4k, so ask() prepends the sentences to the prompt and passes a one-line summary as `context`. Server/plugins/Ask.js is UNTOUCHED, which also means this is live on the owner's server with no restart.

Proven headless at 1280 and 400. Crosshair cursor reads `crosshair`, the outline box matches the hovered rect exactly, Escape clears the overlay and the html class, the picked context resolves readme 2436 chars + decisions 4014 chars, and the wire payload to the server is 7382 chars quoting both files, model haiku, tools empty. At 400 the panel is 364px inside a 400 viewport, no document overflow, no unwanted scrollbar, chip not clipped.

Two real haiku turns spent, both reached the server (two `method: ask` lines in the dev server log) and neither could be read back in the browser: sibling minions saving under public/ triggered LiveReload mid-turn twice, which reloads the headless tab and destroys the panel. That is the known ui-test trap, not a defect in the feature. The wire payload was then proven with a stubbed Socket.request, at zero cost.

assign.outcome:
**Pick any element on a page and ask about it — the answer is handed that page's readme and decisions.**

Open [/framework/ext/Ask/](/framework/ext/Ask/) and click **Pick an element**, then click the card. Nothing is sent and nothing is spent: it prints the context it gathered, with the exact sentences a turn would open with one click down. The floating **?** in the bottom corner of that page is the same thing as a chat.

![the picker mid-hover](picker.jpg)

![the chat panel with the picked element as a chip](chip.jpg)

**What landed**

- `pick()` — crosshair mode, hover outlines, click picks, Escape cancels. Exported from `Ask.js`, written in the new `pick.js`.
- It resolves to the element's **context**: the page url, the element, its markup, and the text of the nearest `readme.md`, the `doc/decisions.md` beside it, and the readme of the framework module that owns its class prefix.
- `ask()` and `chat()` take that context; the turn's prompt opens with plain sentences naming the element, the page and the files, with the files quoted. The chat panel shows a one-line chip naming what the next question is about.
- `mount()` — a floating **?** any page opts into with one call in `content()`. Mounted on the Ask page as the demo. The dev rail's AI tab now has a chat the moment you open it, so its **pick an element** button is there with no thread open.
- Docs: [picking](/framework/ext/Ask/doc/picking/) (the whole mechanism), [decisions](/framework/ext/Ask/doc/decisions/) (the record), [pick](/framework/ext/Ask/api/pick/), readme Use, `doc/file/pick.js.md`.

**No server change.** The element context rides in the prompt, not the system line, because the server caps `context` at 800 characters and a readme is 2,400. `Server/plugins/Ask.js` is untouched — this needs no dev-server restart.

**Left, with the reason**

- `ask-` still needs its line in `framework/styles/css-scopes.txt` (`ask-         ext/Ask`) — that file was outside the write fence. The literal line is in [decisions](/framework/ext/Ask/doc/decisions/) under Open.
- A follow-up question in the same panel resends the whole preamble rather than leaning on the resumed transcript. It keeps the answer grounded and costs pennies; worth changing only if long conversations about one element become normal.
- Two real haiku turns were spent and both reached the CLI, but neither could be read back in the browser: sibling agents saving under `public/` fired LiveReload mid-turn twice and reloaded the headless tab. The wire payload was then proven at zero cost with a stubbed socket — 7,382 characters, quoting both files, model haiku, tools empty.
